external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A person who browses and places orders through the mobile app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application customers use to browse and order socks.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API that stores customer details and hands orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that processes orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that faxes customers a dispatch confirmation.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway
processes.notes: Nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

processes.name: spreadsheet macros
processes.description: Macros in the marketing spreadsheet that send SQL statements to change prices and product copy in the web API.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The database containing customer names, addresses, and the cards they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A file containing delivery addresses and nothing else.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_stores.name: spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The marketing catalogue spreadsheet containing prices and product copy.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: Customer browsing and ordering through the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: place order
data_flows.description: The mobile app places an order with the web API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: keep customer data
data_flows.description: The web API stores customer names, addresses, and payment card details in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_flows.data_description: customer name, address, and payment card

data_flows.name: hand order
data_flows.description: The web API hands an order to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address to the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes the customer a confirmation containing their name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_flows.name: change product copy
data_flows.description: The spreadsheet macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office network location where the marketing laptop and spreadsheet are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app presents a non-web interface because it is explicitly described as a mobile app and there is no website.
assumptions.basis: The source says customers use a mobile app and explicitly says there is no website.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app's SQL-like macro process presents a non-web interface because it is a spreadsheet macro process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes macros in a spreadsheet sending SQL statements, not a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The SIMS process presents a non-web interface because it is described as a stock and inventory system, not a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes SIMS as a stock and inventory system and does not describe it as a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The fax gateway presents a non-web interface because it is a fax gateway.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the component as a fax gateway and describes fax transmission.

assumptions.assumption: The user database is confidential because it contains customer names, addresses, and payment card details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the user database contains customer name, address, and the card they paid with.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file is confidential because it contains delivery addresses, which identify customers.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the flat file contains delivery addresses only.

assumptions.assumption: The marketing spreadsheet macros run in the office because the spreadsheet containing them lives on a marketing laptop in the office.
assumptions.basis: The source says the macros are in the spreadsheet and that the spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.
